summary: Shujun Motegi specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and completed an MA at Kyoto University in 1977. He held posts at Shinshu University, where he is attested as Professor of Ethics in 2010.

Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He held positions at Komazawa University as an assistant, research assistant, and professor, and served as a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University in 1998.
Shuman Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD from Northwestern University in 2014, studying under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn and traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang worked in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies after attending Shuntian Middle School. He joined Peking University's philosophy department in 1917, taught Chun-i Tang, and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and the China Democratic League.

Shun'ei Hirai specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, he taught Noriaki Hakamaya and served at Komazawa University as professor, vice president, and later emeritus professor in 2001.

Shun'ei Mori is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University, attested in 1990, and at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College as a part-time lecturer, attested in 1995.

Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University, serving as professor and emeritus professor at Taisho, and taught Shinjo Kawasaki, Minori Nishimura, and Kosho Kawamura.
Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Shuchiin University, where he is attested as an assistant professor in 1963 and as a professor in 1976.

Shunpei Ueyama worked in philosophy and Japanology, studying at Taihoku High School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University, becoming emeritus professor, and later served as director of Kyoto National Museum and president of Kyoto City University of Arts.

Shunryu Suzuki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji. He served as abbot of Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Soko-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunshō Manabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at Tohoku University, he held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, and taught Lori Meeks.

Shunsuke Tsurumi was a philosopher educated at Middlesex School and Harvard University, where he studied under Willard Van Orman Quine. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Tokyo Institute of Technology, and Doshisha University.
Shuntaro Kondo is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Ryukoku University in 2011 and held an attested post there as a part-time lecturer in 2012.

Shuntarō Matsuyama was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji. He taught at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and served as professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design.

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University in 1993 and served there as associate professor and professor, attested in 1996 and 2005 respectively.

Shuyu Kanaoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, earning a doctorate from Toyo, where he served as an assistant professor from around 1960 to 1992.
Shwe Zan Aung was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon. He pursued traditional studies under U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.

Shōdō Yamagami is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He held positions at Kyoto Sangyo University, serving as assistant professor and later as professor, attested in 1995.
Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from around 1932 to 1936. He later served as a professor at Rissho University, attested in 1972.

Shōyū Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as vice president at Musashino University, attested in 1976, and as chairperson of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism until 1995.
